body: And this was working before that commit was merged?
I should say, what did it do before? (Please note the instructions in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/4900#issuecomment-170288874 for reporting a bug

> The version of ESLint you are using (run eslint -v)

This looks like a regression introduced by 0d50df705f1df2d1486c7fdad14ab0aefd31215f

> What you did (the source code and ESLint configuration)

Here is the source code and complete config (same as in the original description):

```
/* eslint valid-jsdoc: [2, {requireReturn: false}] */

/**
 * Create a new thing.
 */
var thing = new Thing({
  foo: function() {
    return 'bar';
  }
});
```

> The actual ESLint output complete with numbers

```
$ git checkout 0d50df705f1df2d1486c7fdad14ab0aefd31215f
$ node bin/eslint.js --no-eslintrc script.js

/Users/tschaub/projects/eslint/script.js
  3:1  error  Missing JSDoc @returns for function  
```

> What you expected to happen instead

I would expect the above code to be valid according to `valid-jsdoc`.  The documentation block is not associated with the function expression.

Prior to 0d50df705f1df2d1486c7fdad14ab0aefd31215f, the `valid-jsdoc` rule treated this code as valid (as it should):

```
$ git checkout 0d50df705f1df2d1486c7fdad14ab0aefd31215f^
$ node bin/eslint.js --no-eslintrc script.js
$
```

The issue is that the `sourceCode.getJSDocComment()` traverses up to the assignment expression, finds the leading comments, and returns these as the comment associated with the function expression.
